lessons.title: Coordinates and rigid transformations
lessons.summary: Find points on segments and apply and describe reflections, translations and rotations.
lessons.objective: Find points on segments and apply and describe reflections, translations and rotations.
lessons.before: Find the change in x and in y from the first endpoint to the second.
lessons.ideas:
Scale both coordinate changes by the required fraction, then add the changes to the first point.

A reflection across the y-axis changes the sign of x. For translation, add the horizontal and vertical movements separately.

A 90° clockwise turn sends the displacement (a, b) to (b, −a). Add the new displacement to the centre.

A translation has the same movement for every vertex. A rigid sequence of reflections, rotations and translations preserves lengths and angles, so the image is congruent.
lessons.method:
Show the step that explains your answer.

Show the step that explains your answer.

Show the step that explains your answer.

Show the step that explains your answer.
mistakes: A movement gives a pair of changes, not the final location.
Swapping the order of two transformations can change the final position.
A rotation not centred at the origin cannot be read by swapping x and y alone.
An image can face a new way and still have exactly the same side lengths and area.

examples.title: Divide a line segment
examples.question:
Points A and B are (5,3) and (11,-3). P lies one third of the way from A to B.

  1. Give P as an ordered pair.

    [2]

  2. Give the ratio AP : PB.

    [1]
examples.solution:
(a) From A to B, the changes are 6 in x and -6 in y.

Use one third of each change. Add the resulting vector (2, -2) to A.

\((7,1)\)

(b) The first part is one third, leaving two thirds.

1 : 2.

examples.title: Reflect, then translate
examples.question:
Point P starts at (5,4). Reflect it in the y-axis. Then move it 2 units right and 2 units down.

  1. Give the final ordered pair.

    [2]

  2. Would swapping the order give the same point? Explain.

    [2]
examples.solution:
(a) The reflection gives (-5,4).

Add 2 to x and subtract 2 from y.

\((-3,2)\)

(b) Translation and reflection need not commute.

No. Reflecting after translating changes the sign of the rightward movement.

examples.title: Rotate about a marked centre
examples.question:
Rotate point P (7,8) 90° clockwise about centre C (5,6).

  1. Give the coordinates of the image.

    [2]

  2. Explain whether rotating a whole triangle this way would change its side lengths.

    [2]
examples.solution:
(a) Read the movement from C to P as (2, 2).

A clockwise quarter turn sends it to (2, -2).

Add the new movement back to C.

\((7,4)\)

(b) A rigid rotation moves each vertex without stretching its distances to the other vertices.

No. The rotation keeps lengths and angles. The two triangles are congruent.

examples.title: Describe a change from an object to an image
examples.question:
A triangle has vertices (5,7), (7,7) and (5,8). Its corresponding image vertices are (3,5), (5,5) and (3,6).

  1. Give the translation movement as an ordered pair (horizontal change, vertical change).

    [2]

  2. Describe the transformation fully and compare the two areas.

    [2]
examples.solution:
(a) Subtract the original coordinates from the image coordinates. Each vertex moves (-2, -2).

\((-2,-2)\)

(b) Translations preserve both side lengths and angles.

A translation 2 units left and 2 units down. The areas are equal.

lessons.title: Enlargement and changes in area
lessons.summary: Enlarge from a centre, identify a scale factor and compare perimeters and areas.
lessons.objective: Enlarge from a centre, identify a scale factor and compare perimeters and areas.
lessons.before: Mark the centre even when it lies inside or on the edge of the original shape.
lessons.ideas:
With a positive scale factor, each image point stays on the same ray from the centre through its original point.

Extend two distinct vertex-to-image lines to find their intersection. The ratio of image distance to original distance gives the factor.

Each new length is k times its old length. So area is k² times the old area.

Every side changes by the same factor. Add them after scaling, or multiply the old perimeter by that factor.
lessons.method:
Show the step that explains your answer.

Show the step that explains your answer.

Show the step that explains your answer.

Show the step that explains your answer.
mistakes: Use distances from the stated centre, not from the origin unless they are the same point.
The difference between the distances does not give the scale factor.
An enlargement of scale factor 3 multiplies a rectangle's area by 9.
Area and perimeter have different multipliers.

examples.title: Scale distances from a centre
examples.question:
Enlarge a shape by scale factor 5 about (5,3). One vertex is (7,1).

  1. Give the corresponding image coordinates.

    [2]

  2. Explain how to draw the other vertices.

    [2]
examples.solution:
(a) The vertex displacement from the centre is (2, -2).

Multiply both changes by 5, then add them to the centre.

\((15,-7)\)

(b) The same centre and scale factor apply to every vertex.

Draw a ray from the centre through each vertex. Multiply the original distance along each ray by the scale factor.

examples.title: Find the scale factor from one ray
examples.question:
The centre of an enlargement is (7,4). The vertex (9,6) moves to (13,10).

  1. Find the scale factor.

    [2]

  2. Describe how to find an unknown centre with two pairs of corresponding vertices.

    [2]
examples.solution:
(a) The horizontal displacement from the centre changes from 2 to 6. The vertical displacement has the same ratio.

\(3\)

(b) Each original vertex, its image and the centre lie on the same straight line.

Extend the two lines which each join an original vertex to its image. Find their intersection.

examples.title: Compare scale factors of lengths and areas
examples.question:
The rectangle measures 2 cm by 2 cm. It is enlarged by positive scale factor 6.

  1. Find its new area in square centimetres.

    [2]

  2. Give the multiplier for the other measure.

    [1]
examples.solution:
(a) The new sides are 12 cm and 12 cm.

Multiply the two new side lengths.

\(144\)

(b) Perimeter scales by k. Area scales by k squared.

\(6\).

examples.title: Compare scale factors of lengths and areas
examples.question:
The rectangle measures 2 cm by 2 cm. It is enlarged by positive scale factor 4.

  1. Find its new perimeter in centimetres.

    [2]

  2. Give the multiplier for the other measure.

    [1]
examples.solution:
(a) The new sides are 8 cm and 8 cm.

Add the four new side lengths.

\(32\)

(b) Perimeter scales by k. Area scales by k squared.

\(16\).

questions.prompt_html:

  1. Find its new area in square centimetres.

questions.solution_html:

Multiply the two new side lengths.

\(1575\)

\(5\).

questions.title: Scale distances from a centre
questions.prompt_html:
Enlarge a shape by scale factor 4 about (10,11). One vertex is (20,4).

  1. Give the corresponding image coordinates.

    [2]

  2. Explain how to draw the other vertices.

    [2]
questions.answer_html:
(a) \((50,-17)\)

(b) Draw a ray from the centre through each vertex. Multiply the original distance along each ray by the scale factor.
questions.solution_html:
(a) The vertex displacement from the centre is (10, -7).

Multiply both changes by 4, then add them to the centre.

\((50,-17)\)

(b) The same centre and scale factor apply to every vertex.

Draw a ray from the centre through each vertex. Multiply the original distance along each ray by the scale factor.

questions.title: Find the scale factor from one ray
questions.prompt_html:
The centre of an enlargement is (9,5). The vertex (11,13) moves to (13,21).

  1. Find the scale factor.

    [2]

  2. Describe how to find an unknown centre with two pairs of corresponding vertices.

    [2]
questions.answer_html:
(a) \(2\)

(b) Extend the two lines which each join an original vertex to its image. Find their intersection.
questions.solution_html:
(a) The horizontal displacement from the centre changes from 2 to 4. The vertical displacement has the same ratio.

\(2\)

(b) Each original vertex, its image and the centre lie on the same straight line.

Extend the two lines which each join an original vertex to its image. Find their intersection.
questions.hint_html: Compare two matching distances from the centre.

marking_criteria.description_html: Compare two matching distances from the centre.

Extend the two lines which each join an original vertex to its image. Find their intersection.
